clue.text: Advertisement for cake

definitions.meaning: a piece of extravagant promotional praise
a ... is a light pastry, as in cream ...

explanation.definitionFit: Both are standard senses of one short word: overblown promotion, and a light hollow pastry.

clue.text: Noble holding old see or an archbishopric

indicators.note: holding says the noble wraps around the next letters

parts.note: a prince is a noble
V stands for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: A nobleman possessing an ancient see or archbishopric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a bishop's seat but gives V (vide). 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In church organisation a province is the region under an archbishop.

clue.text: One should keep up one's high standard

definitions.text: One should keep up one's high standard

parts.words: One should keep up one's high standard
parts.note: reads like moral advice, but the standard is a flag held aloft

explanation.definitionFit: A flagpole holds a flag (a standard) high in the air.

clue.text: Make way to river past youth hostel, originally a model dwelling

indicators.note: past says the river comes beyond, i.e. after, the other letters

parts.note: to wend is to make one's way

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England (there are several)

explanation.surface: Directions for a walker heading to a river beyond a youth hostel, to see some model house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the first letters of youth and hostel; 'past' puts the river after them. 'to' is just a link, and 'youth hostel' is not a single unit here.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wendy house is a small toy house children play in, a miniature home.

clue.text: Recall a mistake at bridge, not leading king

indicators.note: not leading removes the first letter of the bridge mistake

parts.note: a revoke is failing to follow suit when able, an offence in card games like bridge
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Remembering a bridge error made without leading a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'king' sounds like a card, but it gives R (Rex), taken from the front of REVOKE.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to bring to mind, to call up a memory.

clue.text: Last month, Irish town prematurely ended sporting contest

parts.note: Dec is the standard abbreviation for December, the last month of the year

indicators.note: prematurely ended cuts off the final letter of the town's name

parts.note: Athlone is a town in the middle of Ireland

explanation.surface: An Irish town cut short a sporting event last month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prematurely ended' drops the final E from ATHLONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A decathlon is a ten-event athletics competition.

clue.text: With net, drag Rhine — terribly distressing

indicators.note: terribly suggests the words are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Dredging the Rhine with a net, perhaps for a body, is grim work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges NET, DRAG and RHINE together. 'With' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart-rending means causing great sorrow or anguish.

clue.text: Ruined, as metaphysical poet declared himself

definitions.meaning: John Donne, the metaphysical poet, wrote after his secret marriage 'John Donne, Anne Donne

explanation.definitionFit: Undone means ruined or destroyed, and Donne punned on his own surname.

clue.text: In rising river, perch slowly disappeared

indicators.note: In places the perch inside the river
in a down entry, rising means the river's name reads upwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a perch or rod is an old unit of length

explanation.surface: A fisherman's perch vanished slowly in a rising river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the river upwards in this down entry; 'In' puts the perch inside it. Perch is not a fish here but an old measure of length.
explanation.definitionFit: Eroded means worn away gradually, so slowly gone.

clue.text: Get round bar in Scottish town

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: Advice to get round a pub's bar while visiting a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' is only a link here; round gives O and bar gives BAN. Oban is a port town on Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a real town in Argyll, western Scotland.

clue.text: What racing swimmer should do at the end is uncertain

definitions.text: What racing swimmer should do at the end
definitions.meaning: a racing swimmer must touch the wall at the end of a length and then push off again
an outcome in doubt until the last moment is described by this idiom

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means precarious or risky, with success in doubt right to the end.

clue.text: A sign of uncertainty, to interrogate bookmaker

parts.note: to question someone is to interrogate them
St Mark wrote one of the Gospels, so he made a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: An uneasy punter means to grill a bookie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bookmaker' suggests a bookie, but it is the Gospel writer Mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A question mark is the punctuation symbol that shows doubt or a query.

clue.text: Foolish admission by Mrs. Grundy, not heartless

parts.note: Mrs Grundy, a character from an old English play, is a byword for a narrow-minded prude, so she might admit 'I'm prude'

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter of the word not

parts.note: the word not as written, before losing its middle letter

explanation.surface: Mrs Grundy, the prim moralist, making a foolish confession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle letter from the word not. Mrs Grundy is a prudish character from Thomas Morton's 1798 play Speed the Plough.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means unwise or rash, a synonym of foolish.

clue.text: Cat runs off about noon to find shade

indicators.note: about says what is left of the cat goes round the noon letter
off says the runs letter is dropped from the cat

parts.note: a tiger is a big cat
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cat runs away around midday to find some shade.
explanation.walkthrough: TIGER less R gives TIGE; 'about' puts it round N to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight tint or trace of colour, so a shade.

clue.text: Ignore left-overs of Sunday roast?

definitions.meaning: to snub someone deliberately is the meaning of this idiom
taken literally, a chilled joint of lamb from the shoulder, served the next day

explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the cold shoulder is to rebuff or ignore them pointedly.

clue.text: Bowl poorly, perhaps, but finished with wicket

parts.note: over means finished
in cricket the wicket is also the pitch, the strip played on

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler bowls badly but still takes a wicket in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: To overpitch in cricket is to bowl the ball too far up so it lands too close to the batter; 'perhaps' marks it as one form of poor bowling. 'but' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, overpitching is bowling too full a length, often an error.

clue.text: Noble assembly, with restriction to youthful members?

definitions.meaning: read as three words, a ..., a limit excluding the young

explanation.definitionFit: Baronage is the barons as a class, and split up it reads as a ban on the underage.

clue.text: Leather has strange colour

indicators.note: strange indicates the word has is jumbled

parts.note: green is a colour

explanation.surface: A leather item with an odd colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges the word has, which then goes before the colour. 'Leather' sits at the front as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shagreen is untanned rough-grained leather, often from sharkskin.

clue.text: Two sentences of great importance

definitions.meaning: a court can pass a life sentence or a death sentence
a matter so serious it is vital is described with this phrase

explanation.definitionFit: A 'life-and-death' matter is one of the utmost seriousness.

clue.text: Youngster woman's carrying is an angel

indicators.note: carrying says the youngster holds the woman's letters inside

parts.note: a cub is a young animal or a young Scout
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A mother carrying her baby says the child is an angel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a winged child-like angel in art and scripture.

clue.text: Plant for infusion

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
tea is an infusion of leaves

explanation.surface: A plant grown to make a herbal brew.
explanation.definitionFit: Protea is a South African flowering shrub.

clue.text: Flier I got away from narcotic

indicators.note: got away from says the letter I leaves the drug's name

parts.note: heroin is a narcotic drug

explanation.surface: A drug addict claims to have escaped from narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a bird, and so something that flies.

clue.text: Ordinary boy's introduction to great church music

parts.note: plain means ordinary, unadorned
a boy is a son

indicators.note: introduction to takes the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An ordinary boy is introduced to grand church music.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong is unaccompanied medieval chant used in church liturgy.

clue.text: Came to wonder about agreement

indicators.note: about says the wonder word goes round the agreement word

parts.note: awe is wonder
OK expresses agreement

explanation.surface: Someone surfaced from sleep wondering about a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Came to means regained consciousness, i.e. woke up.

clue.text: Withdrawal from battle after extremes of rage and terror

indicators.note: after places the battle word behind those outer letters
extremes of takes the first and last letters of each of the next two words

parts.note: an action is a military engagement

explanation.surface: A retreat from the battlefield after bouts of rage and terror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of' takes the first and last letters of rage and terror; 'after' puts the battle behind them. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A retraction is a taking back or pulling in, a withdrawal.

clue.text: Chinatown?

parts.note: split into two: a word for china goods that is also the name of a market town in Hertfordshire, England

explanation.definitionFit: Ware means pottery, as in earthenware, and Ware is a town near Hertford.

clue.text: Jacob, for one, isn't such a bad character

definitions.text: Jacob, for one, isn't such a bad character

parts.words: Jacob, for one, isn't such a bad character
parts.note: the Jacob is a piebald breed of sheep with dark fleece, yet it is no family disgrace

explanation.definitionFit: A black sheep is the disreputable member of a family; a Jacob is a literal dark-fleeced sheep.

clue.text: Songwriter needing contribution from backer, naturally

indicators.note: contribution from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A songwriter needs a financial contribution from a backer, of course.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'needing', which is only a link joining definition to wordplay; the songwriter alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerome Kern was an American composer of popular songs and musicals such as Show Boat.
